name: red eye overview
title: Red eye: red flags decide whether it is vision threatening. Without them it is the lids, a conjunctivitis told apart by its discharge and itch, a subconjunctival hemorrhage or a corneal abrasion; with them it is keratitis, anterior uveitis or acute angle closure glaucoma and needs urgent ophthalmology; each column gives the presentation, the exam finding that decides it and the treatment, and a last column for the other vision threats (orbit, sclera, globe)

root.title: Red eye: is it VISION THREATENING?
lines: 2-3% of primary care and emergency visits

red flag symptoms: blurred vision that does NOT clear with blinking (clears = discharge) · SEVERE pain (keratitis, ulcer, iritis, scleritis, glaucoma) · photophobia (iritis) · coloured halos (corneal edema, high pressure)
red flag signs: ↓ acuity · ciliary flush · corneal opacity · abnormal pupil · shallow chamber · ↑ pressure · proptosis

ask: onset, one or both eyes · pain, photophobia · discharge type + amount · itch · vision · recent cold · family member with red eye · contact lenses (swim, sleep, shower in them?) · trauma, eye surgery · eye drops · autoimmune disease

exam: acuity, glasses on, one eye at a time · pupils · eye movements · node in front of the ear, dermatomal rash (zoster) · evert the lid · diffuse redness vs ciliary flush · fluorescein + cobalt blue light · blood (hyphema) or pus (hypopyon) in the chamber, chamber depth

groups.title: NO red flags: lids, conjunctiva, surface
lines: acuity and pressure normal: treat or reassure
• NOT threatening: blepharitis, stye, chalazion, conjunctivitis, dry eye, abrasion, subconjunctival hemorrhage

groups.title: RED FLAGS: vision threatening
lines: • anterior chamber: uveitis, acute angle closure

head: h
Stye · chalazion · entropion
LIDS · also blepharitis, ectropion
pres: • tender red lump, days: STYE (blocked meibomian gland, staph)
inv: • entropion: lid turned in, hazy cornea, epithelial defects
case: 84, nursing home, both eyes red, gritty
tx: • stye or chalazion: refer if not gone in 3-4 weeks or blocks vision
• chalazion: antibiotic-steroid drops, steroid injection (watch pressure), excision
artificial tears + refer for lid surgery · risk of corneal ulcer

head: h
Viral conjunctivitis
CONJUNCTIVA · usually adenovirus
with sore throat, fever
inv: • node in front of the ear
tx: • contagious 10-12 days: hand hygiene, no shared towels
• preservative-free drops 4-8 times a day, cool compresses

head: h
Bacterial conjunctivitis
Staph aureus, Staph epidermidis > Strep pneumoniae, H. influenzae
h
Gonococcal conjunctivitis
or chlamydial
tx: • ceftriaxone 1 g IM + azithromycin 1 g by mouth (chlamydia), once

head: h
Subconjunctival hemorrhage
pres: • trauma · Valsalva: lifting, cough, sneeze, vomiting, straining

head: h
Corneal abrasion
CORNEA · foreign body
tx: • refer only if penetration, hyphema, retained body

head: h
Bacterial keratitis
CORNEA · ulcer · contact lens-related
also herpetic keratitis
pres: case: abrasion treated, back in lenses → 10 days later

head: h
Anterior uveitis (iritis)
ANTERIOR CHAMBER
HLA-B27; ~50% idiopathic
pres: • PAIR: psoriasis, ankylosing spondylitis, IBD, reactive arthritis

head: h
Acute angle closure glaucoma
ANTERIOR CHAMBER
aqueous cannot drain
pres: • female, older, Asian or Inuit, hyperopia, thick lens, family history
tx: topical beta-blocker, alpha-agonist, carbonic anhydrase inhibitor
